spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py:166 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the entire ReAct loop; subject_loop.py:227 sets `traj.hit_turn_cap = (len(traj.turns) >= max_turns)`. cfg.max_turns is threaded through run_battery.py:156 into run_subject. The loop has no other normal termination, so the range() bound actually stops execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced loop bound. Note its stated purpose is measurement (TTI censoring), and the design deliberately keeps the subject going.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 40   # turn cap; also acts as censoring point for TTI

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap is the only hard stop

spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py:166-225: the loop runs the full `range(max_turns)` with no severity/distress-based break. The only other break (subject_loop.py:170-175) is on a client API exception. detect_heuristics/judge_trajectory run AFTER the loop completes (run_battery.py:157-158), so no induction/severity signal ever halts the subject early. spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop is deliberately permissive: it lets the subject keep going (with a turn cap) so unstable behavior has room to surface.

spec_features.notes: Subject file operations cannot reach the host filesystem.

spec_features.spec_quote: we never `exec` subject code... we must not run model-generated code on the host
spec_features.evidence: env.run_tests (env.py:60-74) dispatches only to deterministic archetype methods (_contradictory, _moving_target, etc.) that pattern-match on file text and never exec/eval. grep confirms no exec/eval/subprocess/os.system anywhere in the codebase; subject-written content in env.files is only string-inspected.
spec_features.notes: Subject-generated code is never executed; tests are simulated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No real code execution; "tests" are deterministic checks the env controls.
